name: Easton Royal
strengths: Royal's best tape trait is YAC — once he clears the first tackle angle he has a second gear that pulls away from pursuit.
Royal's listed 5-11 / 200 looks real on film: thick lower half, stays on his feet through arm tackles, and finishes runs with contact balance.
Royal is used as a true weapon — split wide, slot, and in the screen/jet-touch game — not a one-alignment perimeter guy.
weaknesses: Highlight cuts emphasize space YAC more than full stems vs press; route polish and contested high-point sample need more all-22 before locking those claims.
comparison: Royal comps to Deebo Samuel — 5-11 / 6-0 thick WR mold; sudden after the catch, contact balance, and enough mass to punish tackle angles (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Royal projects as a Year 1 package/special-teams WR (screens, manufactured touches), Year 2 rotation slot/flex, with Year 3 every-down starter ceiling as a physical YAC weapon — not a pure length X.
schemeFit: Royal fits Faulkner as a boundary/slot hybrid built for manufactured touches and YAC after the catch.
